extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, litigators, judges, and advanced law students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the issuance, scope, duration, violation, dissolution, and contempt remedies for preliminary injunctions in patent litigation. Focused on procedural and substantive rules courts apply when granting, enforcing, or dissolving injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction takes effect according to its terms
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction takes effect according to its terms, and operates only upon the persons and the actions named therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It remains in force as long as the patent is capable of infringement, unless previously recalled by the court or superseded by some other judgment in the suit. It has no authority over acts or individuals beyond the local jurisdiction of the court except as otherwise provided by jurisdictional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration — limited to life and capability of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction will remain in force as long as it may be needed and can run only during the life of the patent and should be so limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be modified from time to time, continued under a re-issue by supplemental bill, or suspended temporarily in public emergencies or extraordinary necessity. If the date of expiration is in dispute the court will not limit the injunction, but the defendant may move for dissolution when the date he claims has arrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial and personal jurisdiction limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction has no authority over acts or individuals beyond the local jurisdiction of the court except where the court obtains jurisdiction over the defendant's person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defendant residing and infringing in one district cannot be enjoined by the court of another if the injunction would be ineffective; process runs against the person, and the court may award it though it gives the plaintiff no effectual relief. The court may restrain use in another district only if it has obtained jurisdiction over the defendant's person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction must be restricted to things named
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction must be restricted to the things named therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will limit orders to the scope explicitly described in the decree; overbroad injunctions may be subject to prompt motion to set aside or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds/security when enjoining vendees or when cross-jurisdiction issues arise
rubrics_metrics.description: When a plaintiff is enjoined from suing the defendant's vendees, or when the court's injunction may give no effectual relief, the defendant must give bonds to secure the plaintiff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where process runs against parties outside the district or relief is potentially ineffective, bonds are often required to protect the enjoined party from loss if injunction proves improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction may be continued under re-issue by supplemental bill
rubrics_metrics.description: If an injunction lapses through the surrender of the patent for re-issue, it may be continued under the re-issue by an order granted on a supplemental bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties seeking continuation after re-issue must file supplemental pleadings; courts treat re-issued patents and injunctions specially and may continue relief where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction may be suspended in public emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction may be suspended temporarily in public emergencies, or when extraordinary necessity arises outside the private interests of the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have discretion to suspend injunctions for compelling public reasons, separate from the private equities between the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions and expiration disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the date of the expiration of the patent is in dispute the court will not limit the injunction, but the defendant can move for a dissolution when the date at which he claims the patent must expire has arrived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts avoid prematurely narrowing injunctions when expiration is contested; defendants have remedy to seek dissolution at the proper time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for dissolution — invalidity, lack of title, justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary injunction may be dissolved when evidence on the merits shows that the patent is invalid, or the plaintiff without title, or the acts of the defendant justifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On application for dissolution the defendant bears the burden of proof; where the injunction was supported by patents, judgments and prior injunctions 'only the most conclusive evidence' can overturn it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's burden and standard to dissolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the application for dissolution the defendant has the burden of proof, and if the injunction were granted on the oath of the plaintiff fortified by patent, judgments, acquiescence, and former injunctions, only the most conclusive evidence can prevail upon the court to reverse its former decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendants must present strong, convincing proof (e.g., prior knowledge, prior art, or conclusive evidence) to overcome previous findings and maintain dissolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution on evidence of prior knowledge/prior device
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction will be dissolved on evidence showing that the device was known in the United States before the patent, and on the production of the device itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production of a prior device or convincing proof of prior public knowledge/use is a classic ground for dissolving a preliminary injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: License from patentee as ground for dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the defendant acts under a license from the plaintiff the injunction will be dissolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license (conditional or unconditional) by the patentee that justifies the defendant's actions will typically defeat injunctive relief against that defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors not normally justifying dissolution (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction will not be dissolved on the ground of hardship to the defendant when he knowingly infringed, nor on account of a conditional license granted to him by the plaintiff, nor for informality in the notice if the defendant actually appeared, nor on doubts as to the powers of Patent Office officials when legislation is pending to remove them, nor on the same evidence which induced the court to grant it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere hardship, stale doubts about PTO procedures, procedural informality cured by appearance, or re-argument of the same proof that produced the injunction are generally insufficient to obtain dissolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to dissolve — balance of equities and evidence weighing
rubrics_metrics.description: On a motion to dissolve the court must weigh the evidence, and if the balance is in favor of the plaintiff continue the injunction and allow an action at law to be brought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissolution is an equitable determination; the trial court weighs competing proofs and may keep injunctive relief in place while directing other remedies (e.g., damages trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where validity is disputed — requirement to bring action at law
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the defendants in equity dispute the validity of the patent, a suit at law must be brought at the next term, or the pending injunction will be dissolved; on such suit the trial will be confined to the objections set up in the answer and affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable injunctions are not the place to re-litigate all validity issues indefinitely; defendants may be required to seek their legal remedies in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informality cured by appearance; failure to take proofs fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: On a motion to dissolve an injunction, informality in serving notice is considered cured by the appearance of the defendant; conversely, where the plaintiff has taken proofs and the defendant none, and the defendant moves to dissolve without asking leave to amend, the motion will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural posture and diligence in taking proofs affect dissolution motions — failure to present proofs earlier and to amend may preclude relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obey injunction until rescinded
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction, whether granted on an ex parte or a contested hearing, or by consent, is binding on the defendant, and must be obeyed until rescinded by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defendant cannot construe the injunction for himself or continue portions of the practice; he must desist wholly from the practice of the invention and apply to the court for further instructions if needed. Advice of counsel or good faith belief does not excuse violation, though it may affect penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: No self-help experimentation to avoid infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant has no right to experiment with other arts or instruments to see how nearly he can imitate the plaintiff's and still escape infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts treat deliberate attempts to evade an injunction (colorable variations, evasive processes) as violations; counsel's advice does not protect from contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: How an injunction is violated — acts constituting contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction is violated by the participation of the defendant in any manufacture, use, or sale of the invention, contrary to the language or the spirit of the prohibition; no cover or subterfuge affords immunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation occurs whether the defendant acts as principal, agent, or workman, whether he completes the article or sends it elsewhere to be finished, and includes employing evasive processes or colorable variations. Good faith differences may be relevant but do not automatically absolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers of ownership or dispositions are contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transaction which passes the ownership of the forbidden articles from the defendant to another person, whether alone or incorporated into other articles — whether under the form of a sale, a barter, a mortgage, or a judgment — if voluntarily entered into and performed by the defendant, is a defiance of the prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agreement to sell without delivery or intent to deliver is not contempt, but any completed transfer after the injunction that passes ownership is contempt. Permitting others to make or use or sell on defendant's behalf is also contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of separately claimed parts
rubrics_metrics.description: To use a separately claimed part of the invention is a contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even partial practice of claimed elements (if separately claimed) can violate an injunction forbidding the invention; courts have held that using separately claimed parts may be punished as contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith use of different patents or post-expiration devices may not be contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of articles covered by different patents and not obviously identical with the enjoined invention, if in good faith, is not a contempt of the injunction; nor is the employment of devices made after the plaintiff's patent had expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the articles are 'obviously the same' or if identity is shown, good-faith assertions are insufficient; the factual question of identity controls whether contempt exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction may be violated by agents, officers, servants, or persons under control
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction may be violated not only by the acts of the defendant himself, but by those of other persons representing him or under his control; an injunction against a city binds its public boards if they have notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers of corporations, sons or servants acting under control, managers of related corporations, and agents who infringe after notice can be held for contempt; notice and control are key factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendee of infringing business not bound unless party
rubrics_metrics.description: The vendee of the defendant's infringing business, pending suit, is not bound by an injunction afterwards obtained unless he were made a party to the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers of ownership do not automatically bind successors unless they are joined in the litigation or otherwise bound by the decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for violation — application for attachment for contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy of the plaintiff for the violation of an injunction is by an application to the court for an order of attachment against the defendant; this application is collateral and may be made any time when the misconduct renders it necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must state the specific acts or omissions constituting contempt; interrogatories must be confined to those offences; the defendant need not answer matters charged on information and belief and may demur to improper interrogatories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of contempt proceeding — no re-litigation of patent construction or validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the hearing on an application for attachment no new evidence can be received to vary the construction already given to the patent, nor can the defendant attack the validity of the injunction; the only point at issue is the performance by the defendant of the forbidden acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alleged violation raises a new question of identity between the defendant's device and the patented invention, or requires re-examination of construction or validity, that matter is inappropriate for summary contempt proceedings and requires new pleadings, a supplemental bill, or separate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment is summary relief; new issues require full suit
rubrics_metrics.description: An attachment is intended only for summary relief where the single issue raised relates to the commission by the defendant of the prohibited acts; collateral or fundamental questions cannot be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion for attachment will not be granted if the claim that the injunction has been violated raises a new question as to the construction of the patent, because on that question the defendant has a right to be heard; the court may examine infringement for contempt but that decision does not prejudice the parties on the accounting.
